findings.problem: The PR summary says "punctuation is dropped", but `sentenceWords` only removes trailing . , ! ? from each word. Other punctuation stays, for example titleCase('it\'s (fine)') gives "It's (fine)". The code matches WORDS-021; only the PR wording overstates what it does.
findings.fix: In the PR summary, say that trailing . , ! ? are dropped instead of all punctuation.

end.reason: The diff is empty and the code matches WORDS-021. Only the PR description is slightly loose, so it isn't worth a ticket.

findings.problem: WORDS-022 says each later word gets 'the rest lower-cased', but no test puts an upper-case letter in a later word. 'NASA' is the first word, and 'rocks' and 'really' are already lower-case, so the `.toLowerCase()` in src/case/camel.js:7 is only checked on the first word.
findings.fix: Add an assertion with a mixed-case later word, for example `camelCase('hello WORLD')` should give `'helloWorld'`.

findings.problem: The README doesn't say that the four conversions leave text that is already joined as one word. So `snakeCase('helloWorld')` gives `'helloworld'`, not `'hello_world'`. Punctuation inside a word also stays: `kebabCase('a,b c')` gives `'a,b-c'`. Someone reading only the README would likely expect the opposite in both cases. The ticket leaves this out of scope on purpose, so the code is right; only the docs are silent.
findings.fix: Add one line under the four conversions: "Text already in camelCase or snake_case stays one word (`snakeCase('helloWorld')` gives `'helloworld'`), and only trailing `. , ! ?` are dropped."

findings.problem: There are now two ways to make dash-joined text, and they give different results. The existing `slugify` (src/slug.js) splits words with `splitWords`, so it keeps punctuation: `slugify('Hi, there!')` gives `'hi,-there!'`. The new `kebabCase` drops it and gives `'hi-there'`. The README lists only `kebabCase`. Separately, when the planned comma splitting (WORDS-012, specified but not yet built) lands in `splitWords`, it will quietly change the output of all four conversions, because they get their words through `sentenceWords`, which calls `splitWords`. For example, `kebabCase('a,b c')` would change from `'a,b-c'` to `'a-b-c'`.
findings.fix: No code change in this milestone. Add a line to CONTRIBUTING.md under Traps: "Changing `splitWords` or `sentenceWords` changes `slugify` and all four case conversions too; rerun their tests and update the README examples. `slugify` keeps punctuation and `kebabCase` drops it, so don't treat them as the same. Learned: SAN-32 capstone. Retire: when `slugify` is removed or built on `kebabCase`."
